author: devbig030
body:
ROOT-CAUSED (2026-09-11, tg layered-arbitrary-rtapp-workload, at integration@426d85e / scx 59c30bae). The guess in the description -- "ops.dispatch is not delivered to an already-idle CPU" -- is WRONG. ops.dispatch IS delivered: handle_task_wake loops over every idle CPU after an enqueue, and try_dispatch_and_run calls it whenever the local DSQ is empty. The bug is an ORDERING divergence from the kernel on the slice-expiry path.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS. engine.rs::stop_and_reenqueue does: stopping() -> ops.enqueue(prev) -> try_dispatch_and_run -> ops.dispatch(cpu, prev). The kernel's balance_one() does the OPPOSITE: ops.dispatch(cpu, prev) runs FIRST with prev still SCX_TASK_QUEUED and NOT yet placed in any DSQ; put_prev_task_scx() (which is what calls do_enqueue_task/ops.enqueue) runs only AFTER pick_task_scx() has decided prev is being switched out.

That ordering matters because of the check balance_one() makes immediately after ops.dispatch returns:

    if (prev_on_rq && prev->scx.slice) { rq->scx.flags |= SCX_RQ_BAL_KEEP; goto has_tasks; }

i.e. if the BPF scheduler refreshed prev's slice from inside ops.dispatch, the kernel KEEPS RUNNING prev and never enqueues it. pick_task_scx() then returns prev because SCX_RQ_BAL_KEEP is set.

layered uses exactly that idiom. keep_running() (main.bpf.c) ends with scx_bpf_task_set_slice(p, layer->slice_ns); return true, and layered_dispatch then returns WITHOUT dispatching anything -- its own comment says "Let's not dispatch any task if we want to keep running @prev. This will trigger the automatic local enq behavior which will put @prev on @cpu's local DSQ." scxsim never implements that behaviour, so the task scxsim already pushed onto the layer DSQ is left there and no CPU comes back for it.

TRACE EVIDENCE (4 CPUs, 3x run-once 20ms, default catch-all, p->tgid = pid applied):

  20003717 cpu2 PutPrevTask { pid: 2, still_runnable: true }
  20003717 cpu2 DsqInsertVtime { pid: 2, dsq_id: 0, slice: 20000000 }   <- enqueue happened FIRST
  20003717 cpu2 EnqueueTask { pid: 2, enq_flags: 0 }
  20003717 cpu2 DsqNrQueued { dsq_id: 0x40000000, ret: 0 }              <- the hi_fb probe INSIDE keep_running()
  20003767 cpu2 Balance { prev_pid: Some(2) }                           <- dispatch returned having consumed nothing
  20003767 cpu2 CpuIdle

Contrast a healthy dispatch on the same run (cpu0 @14514709): DsqMoveToLocal(hi_fb) / DsqNrQueued(lo_fb) / DsqMoveToLocal(layer 0) / DsqMoveToLocal(lo_fb). The stalled one bails after the hi_fb count -- that is keep_running() returning true.

FALSIFICATION (this is the proof, not the reading). keep_running() starts "if (cpuc->yielding || !max_exec_ns) goto no;". Setting max_exec_ns = 0 in schedulers/layered/wrapper.c (line ~2328) with p->tgid = pid still applied makes default_config_loads_and_runs PASS 3/3. Reverting it fails 2/3 again.

WHY N=3 FAILS AND N=8/N=16 PASS -- the description's own data now explains itself. keep_running()'s open-layer branch is "has_idle = !bpf_cpumask_empty(idle_cpumask)". At N=3 on 4 CPUs there IS an idle CPU, so keep_running() fires and the task is lost. At N=8/16 no CPU is idle, keep_running() returns false, and dispatch proceeds normally. The undersubscribed-only signature is a direct consequence, not a coincidence.

SCOPE. Not a layered bug and not DSQ-id-related. Any scheduler that refreshes prev's slice from inside ops.dispatch hits it. Antistall did not rescue it because antistall_consume() runs at the TOP of layered_dispatch and this CPU's dispatch IS being invoked -- it just returns early below that point; and the task's runnable_at delay is measured in seconds while the run is 200ms.

THE FIX (not applied here; this is workload-language task B, and this is a core-engine change with a blast radius across every scheduler and every timing-sensitive test). Reorder the stop_and_reenqueue spine to match balance_one: stopping() -> ops.dispatch(cpu, prev) with prev NOT yet enqueued -> if prev is still queued and its slice is now non-zero, keep running prev and skip the enqueue entirely -> otherwise ops.enqueue(prev) and continue as today. Note this is ALSO a standalone Principle-1 fidelity debt independent of the stall: scxsim currently calls ops.enqueue on a preempted task before ops.dispatch has been given the chance to claim it, which no kernel does.

Unblocks sim-6mheb (p->tgid = pid) and, through it, the tgid half of sim-ttaa0.
